business_scope.primary_industry_name: Automated Global Payroll and Staff Compliance Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (with Samoan customary law elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa-China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (in force 2014)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus, signed 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (No. 6 of 2007), as amended by the Money Laundering Prevention (Amendment) Act 2017; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2007; International Companies Act 1987 (No. 15 of 1987), as amended; International Companies (Amendment) Regulations 2016; SIFA AML/CFT Guidance Notes applicable to licensed international company service providers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport of each UBO, director, and shareholder of record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the country of residence or origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, issued within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or issuing bank in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Individual bank reference letter confirming account relationship and good standing
Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified constitutional documents of any corporate shareholder (MOA/AOA or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary or corporate registry of formation jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional curriculum vitae and proof of identity for the proposed director(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the director's jurisdiction of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement and continuous screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit consolidated list, United Nations Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, HM Treasury sanctions list, and applicable PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, any person linked to a sanctioned jurisdiction, or any medium-risk/AML-sensitive business classification. Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence must be secured for all high-risk or enhanced-risk profiles.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Name Clearance Portal (agent-accessible via licensed registered agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be rendered in Latin script; English and Samoan are the principal registry languages. A name in Chinese or another non-Latin script may be registered only as a supplementary trade name after a Latin-script phonetic transliteration is submitted for clearance. The registered name must not be misleading, must include a corporate suffix (e.g., Limited, Incorporated), and must not imply a licensed activity without ministerial consent.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banking, Building Society, Trust, Trustee, Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Fiduciary, Fund, Investment Fund, Exchange, Financial Services (each requires prior ministerial approval and evidence of a relevant license)
Government, State, National, Reserve, Central Bank, Sovereign, Crown (prohibited in any form that implies state authority)
Samoa, Samoan, or any geographical derivative used as a standalone or misleading component absent SIFA consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant's licensed registered agent may file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice. If rejected on review, the applicant may lodge an administrative appeal to the head of the Samoa International Finance Authority within 30 days. The decision of SIFA may thereafter be challenged by way of judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible: the International Company must maintain a registered office in Samoa at the physical address of its licensed registered agent. A PO Box alone is not accepted, and no separate physical office in Samoa is required for the operation of a Payroll-SaaS platform under the ISIC 6201 scope.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (less than 5% annual probability) in the absence of adverse intelligence, unusual transaction activity, or PEP-related risk factors. Any on-site inspection would generally be directed at the registered agent's records rather than the company's servers or offshore operations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory extension tariff under the International Companies (Fees) Regulations

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies Amendment Acts 2015 and 2020; incorporation provisions at ss. 4-7 and 44-49; s. 8 (name restrictions); s. 33 (registered office); s. 38 (registered agent); ss. 50-62 (directors and secretary). Subsidiary delegated legislation: International Companies (Fees) Regulations and SIFA AML/CFT Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), International Companies Registry, Apia, Samoa; SIFA is the statutory regulator established under the International Finance Authority Act 2012.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form INC-1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company, accompanied by executed Memorandum and Articles of Association; the Registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation of an International Company on approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The Memorandum must declare authorized share capital (customarily USD 100,000) and at least one share at par value USD 1.00 must be issued to the subscriber. The USD 700 government fee covers authorized capital up to USD 1,000,000. No escrow deposit or paid-up capital funding requirement applies under the International Companies Act 1987.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company under the International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa) be and is hereby adopted; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the allotment of shares to the subscriber as set forth in the Register of Members be approved; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office as maintained by the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa be adopted as the statutory registered office; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed first Director and [Name] be appointed first Secretary, each to serve until removal or retirement under the Articles; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Director be authorized to execute all filings and engage professional advisors to procure the Certificate of Incorporation and tax exemptions for the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA International Companies Registry (lodged through an SIFA-licensed Registered Agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names, or request an SIFA-issued number name, to the licensed Registered Agent. The agent conducts a search of the SIFA index of existing international companies. A name will be rejected if it is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, or implies sovereignty, government patronage, or a restricted regulated activity. Approved names are reserved for 90 days pending full incorporation.
required_dossiers: Name clearance application letter
Three proposed corporate names in priority order
Short description of intended payroll software business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the Registered Agent immediately re-files a substitute name list within the same application; there is no quasi-judicial appeal at the pre-incorporation stage, so the remedy is administrative re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Licensed Registered Agent and AML/KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed Registered Agent (private licensee supervised by SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Registered Agent engagement agreement and complete SIFA-compliant AML/CFT due diligence. The agent must verify the identity of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners, and obtain source-of-funds evidence. Under the International Companies Amendment Act 2020, a declaration of beneficial ownership will be filed with SIFA at or immediately after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Registered agent engagement letter and fee schedule
Certified passport copies of directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months)
Bank reference or professional referee letter
Source of funds statement and AML/CFT questionnaire
Corporate ownership chart where a corporate shareholder is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KYC documentation is rejected as insufficient, the applicant supplies notarized translations, updated dated documents, or an expanded corporate ownership chart; re-submission within 5 business days avoids triggering a fresh suspicion report to the SIFA Financial Intelligence Unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent and intending subscriber (signing parties)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English in accordance with the International Companies Act 1987. The Memorandum must state the company name, registered office in Samoa, registered agent identity, authorized share capital, and limitation of liability; the Articles govern share classes, director powers, and indemnity. The subscriber executes the Memorandum in the presence of a witness or by the Registered Agent as attorney-in-fact. Conclude the subscription for at least one share at USD 1.00 par value.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Share subscription form and allocation schedule
Consent to act as first director and first secretary
Form RO-1 – Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries any non-conforming constitutional clause, instruct counsel to prepare an amending rider or substituted Memorandum; the applicant re-executes the affected pages without losing the name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registered Agent submits Form INC-1, the executed Memorandum and Articles, director and secretary consents, and Form RO-1 to the SIFA Registry electronically or by physical lodgement. Concurrently, remit the USD 700 government incorporation fee plus any capital fee to the SIFA-designated Government of Samoa account by SWIFT transfer, attaching the agent's transmittal letter and payment instruction.
required_dossiers: Form INC-1 – Application for Incorporation
Certified copy of executed Memorandum and Articles
Form RO-1 – Notice of Registered Office and Registered Agent
Consent forms of first director and first secretary
SWIFT wire confirmation for government fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the Registry issues a query sheet identifying defects; the agent files corrective instruments within 14 days, failing which the file lapses and the fee is refundable less the administrative deduction under the International Companies (Fees) Regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Opening of Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: On satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation effective as of the stated date and time, conferring legal personality. The Registered Agent then opens the statutory registers (members, directors, secretary, charges), issues share certificates, prepares the corporate kit, and, if elected, arranges a common seal.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by SIFA)
Register of Members with share allotment entries
Register of Directors and Secretary
Register of Charges
Share certificates and corporate kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a clerical error in the company name or date, file a Request for Reissue with the SIFA Registry together with the defective Certificate; administrative correction is completed within 2 business days at no additional government fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Exemption Confirmation and Compliance Calendar Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA, the Registered Agent, and, where relevant, the Ministry of Revenue of Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the automatic tax-exempt status of the International Company under Part XV of the International Companies Act 1987, which exempts income, capital gains, and stamp duty on international business. Instruct the Registered Agent to calendar the annual SIFA license renewal fee before the anniversary of incorporation, maintain the beneficial ownership register, and assess whether any economic substance filing applies to the foreign-source payroll processing revenue. Use the certified Certificate and statutory registers to open the operational bank account for the payroll SaaS platform.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (certified copy)
Declaration of beneficial ownership filed with SIFA
Annual license fee calendar and SIFA renewal invoice
Economic substance notification or exemption memorandum
Bank account opening pack for the Samoa IC
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Revenue or a bank queries the exemption, furnish the Certificate of Incorporation and the Part XV exemption clause; no annual income tax return is required for International Companies, and the remedy is a confirmatory letter from the Registered Agent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for an offshore International Company providing ISIC 6201 automated payroll software. If the company ever establishes a physical domestic presence, the relevant authority would be the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Business Licences Division, under the Business Licences Act 1998, Schedule of Exemptions.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – no sectoral operating license, manufacturing permit, or financial services license applies to the Payroll SaaS platform; the Certificate of Incorporation, together with the ISIC 6201 services contract structure, constitutes sufficient authorization.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – pure digital software operation with no physical development, manufacturing, or waste-generating activity; not listed in Schedule 1 of the Planning and Urban Management (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations, and no EIA report or EIA registration is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable in substance. To the extent the company leases an office in Samoa, general wastewater discharge complies with Samoa Water Authority sewer standards, and any electronic waste is disposed through licensed contractors under the Waste Management Act 2005. No VOC, NOx, or effluent discharge limits apply to a virtualized payroll processing platform.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If a physical Samoa office is opened, obtain a Fire Clearance Certificate from the Samoa National Fire Services Authority under the Fire and Emergency Services Act; secure building compliance approval from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI) under the Building Code of Samoa; and register as an employer with the Accident Compensation Corporation (Samoa) under the Accident Compensation Act 1983 for occupational injury coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Ministry of Finance – official portal: https://www.sra.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Samoa International Company is statutorily exempt from income tax and is not required to obtain a standard tax identification number. For optional VAGST registration, the company must submit the VAGST registration application (Form VAGST-1) to the Samoa Revenue Authority together with its International Company certificate of incorporation, certificate of registered office, local registered agent details, and estimated annual turnover declaration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - International Companies are automatically exempt under the International Companies Act 1987; no check-the-box, hybrid mismatch, or elective tax classification regime is available under Samoan law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 50,000 annual taxable turnover threshold (mandatory registration); voluntary registration available at lower turnover for certain persons.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate exists. Samoa VAGST relies on conventional invoicing; standard VAT invoices may be issued manually or electronically, but no government API clearance or e-invoicing validation system is currently enforced.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated at 0% VAGST applies to (i) tangible goods exported from Samoa under a contract of sale and removed from Samoa by the supplier; and (ii) services performed in Samoa that are supplied to a non-resident customer located outside Samoa, provided the services are not directly related to land in Samoa or goods situated in Samoa at the time of supply, and do not involve offshore gambling or gaming.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank FX credit record evidencing payment in the required currency
Tax invoice issued under VAGST Act showing 0% rate and export basis
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claims are subject to VAGST reassessment, interest accrual, and penalties under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act. Knowingly providing false export documentation can attract fines up to WST 50,000 and/or imprisonment. The Samoa Revenue Authority may retrospectively claw back input tax credits and zero-rating benefits for up to 8 years in cases of wilful non-disclosure or deliberate misstatement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; CBS administers Samoa's exchange control regime under the Exchange Control Act 1976 through CBS-licensed authorized dealers, supervises all licensed financial institutions, and houses the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) established under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a managed-float currency officially quoted against a trade-weighted basket of major trading-partner currencies, and Samoa has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations, so current-account payments are freely convertible without CBS permit. Capital-account transactions by resident domestic companies require prior CBS approval through an authorized dealer, and profit remittance by resident non-IC companies to non-residents is subject to application and, where applicable, 15% non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 2012. The WS_IC (an International Company under the International Companies Act 1987, as amended, 'ICA') is statutorily exempt from Samoan exchange control and from all Samoan taxes, which removes the CBS approval step and the tax-clearance hurdle entirely; the IC may hold and freely transfer USD/EUR/AUD/NZD accounts with no convertibility restriction, provided it does not carry on business in Samoa with Samoan residents, does not hold interests in Samoan land, and keeps full beneficial-ownership records with its SIFSA-licensed registered agent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies to the WS_IC: because the IC is exempt from the Exchange Control Act 1976, 100% of export receipts and SaaS subscription revenues may be retained in foreign currency, held offshore, or remitted to the IC's multi-currency account at a CBS-licensed authorized dealer without conversion to WST. For completeness, domestic Samoan goods exporters (resident companies, not ICs) operate under CBS exchange-control directions requiring repatriation of export proceeds through an authorized dealer within the prescribed period commonly fixed at 6 months from the date of export, and CBS may direct the authorized dealer to purchase a specified portion of those proceeds in WST; no fixed statutory conversion percentage is published, and the obligation does not extend to the WS_IC.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited (successor to Westpac Bank Samoa Limited)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency Operating Account (USD/EUR/AUD/NZD/WST) and Capital Escrow/Term Deposit Account
Multi-currency Operating Account with SWIFT corporate e-banking and FX dealing desk
WST-denominated Operational Account for domestic registered-agent fees and SIFSA/CBS administrative payments
Local WST Operational Account - retail/domestic focus with limited cross-border treasury capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: MEDIUM as a supplementary payments rail, not as the primary treasury or escrow bank. A properly licensed offshore EMI (e.g., FCA-, ASIC- or EU-supervised electronic money institution) may hold USD/EUR/AUD payment accounts for the WS_IC and execute high-volume payroll-disbursement rails to global client employees and subcontractors where correspondent-bank access of Samoan banks is limited. Legal constraints: (i) no offshore EMI may take deposits from or lend to Samoan residents or maintain WST-denominated customer accounts unless separately CBS-licensed; (ii) an EMI is not a CBS authorized dealer, so it cannot provide FX conversion or document the exchange-control exemption; (iii) all escrow, capital-injection, and hedge settlement flows must remain at a CBS-licensed authorized dealer; (iv) the EMI account must be disclosed to the Samoan bank during onboarding to maintain a coherent flow-of-funds audit trail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Samoan statute requires directors or UBOs to appear physically in Apia for IC account opening. Remote onboarding is permitted where the IC is introduced by a SIFSA-licensed registered agent in good standing and submits: certified certificate of incorporation and good standing, memorandum and articles, register of directors and shareholders (or registered-agent certificate as to beneficial ownership), notarized and consularized or apostilled passports, certified board resolutions opening the account and designating signatories, and bank reference letters. In practice, BSP Samoa and ANZ Samoa require at least one signatory to complete a live video KYC interview, may require the registered agent to co-sign the account mandate, and reserve the right to schedule a physical meeting or on-site verification when the UBO chain includes high-risk jurisdictions, PEPs, or bearer-share history; physical attendance is therefore rarely mandatory but should be treated as a contingency in the onboarding timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company with nominee directors/offshore trust ownership presenting a shell-company or concealment indicator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-agent certificate (SIFSA-licensed) confirming physical registered office and agent; current certificate of good standing from the Samoa Registrar of International and Foreign Companies; certified share register flowing through to natural-person UBOs; corporate-ownership and trust-structure chart to the ultimate individuals; apostilled/notarized passports and utility bills of all UBOs; source-of-wealth statement with supporting bank and investment statements; two independent professional references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, multi-jurisdiction payment flows inherent to a payroll-SaaS platform (receipt of client funds followed by rapid disbursement to employees/subcontractors) assessed as potential structuring or layering under transaction monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed B2B SaaS and payroll-services agreements with the client base; ISIC 6201 revenue-model narrative; platform architecture diagram showing the flow of funds from client remittance to gross-pay disbursement and the IC's fee margin; employer/employee payroll schedules and audit trail; SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent IT-control attestation; a sanctions-screening policy demonstrating exclusion of prohibited jurisdictions; agreed transaction-monitoring thresholds with the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparties or remitters in FATF grey-listed or high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., payments routed through third-country payment aggregators) raising enhanced-due-diligence triggers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative media/PEP screening reports for each UBO and material counterparty; geolocation and business-registration evidence demonstrating genuine operational nexus; a no-tolerance sanctions policy and country-exclusion list; EDD files for each higher-risk counterparty; Samoan-counsel legal opinion confirming the IC's lawful structure and recommending continued banking; AML/CFT questionnaire executed by the board.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital escrow credit from a third-party or group entity without a clean equity chain documentation, queried as unexplained wealth injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorizing allotment; share-allotment letter and issued share certificates; extract from the share register; source-of-funds letter from the remitting shareholder's own bank; acknowledgment that no third party lends funds without a documented loan agreement; confirmation in the remittance narrative that the payment is equity subscription for the ISIC 6201 platform.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route all equity injections by SWIFT MT103 from each shareholder's own account to the WS_IC multi-currency account at a CBS-licensed authorized dealer (BSP Samoa or ANZ Samoa) in USD/EUR with remittance narrative 'EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION - WS_IC - ISIC 6201 PAYROLL PLATFORM'. No CBS exchange-control permit and no Foreign Investment Certificate is required because the ICA exempts the IC from the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the IC is prohibited from domestic business activity; the receiving bank will nevertheless require the allotment board resolution, share-register extract, UBO declaration, and source-of-funds letter prior to crediting. The use of an offshore EMI as an interim receiving vehicle is disfavored for capital injection because the Samoan bank must see a clean remitter-to-beneficiary equity chain to avoid reclassification of the credit as third-party liability.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border outflows (software licensing, cloud-hosting fees, subcontractor coding fees, payroll disbursement to global client employees where the IC is the payer, and group management charges) clear by SWIFT MT103 corporate payment or MT202/MT202 COV bank-to-bank cover in USD/EUR/AUD. For material implementation contracts, an irrevocable documentary credit issued by SWIFT MT700 (and amended by MT707) with a confirming bank is permissible where the counterparty requires LC security; standby LCs (MT760) may back software-delivery obligations. Client-facing payroll disbursements in the United States and the Eurozone execute through the platform's Direct Debit/ACH rails at the offshore EMI or regional processor, with net treasury settlement swept to the Samoan account via SWIFT MT103; the Samoan bank is used for the IC's own corporate outflows and FX/hedge settlement. Domestic WST disbursements (registered-agent fees, SIFSA annual fees, CBS-related administrative charges) settle through the CBS-operated national payment system in WST from a dedicated WST sub-account, either by direct debit or EFT instruction; the IC must pre-fund the WST sub-account by minimal FX conversion and is not expected to maintain WST balances beyond administrative needs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forwards (USD/WST, EUR/USD, USD/AUD and AUD/WST) executed with onshore CBS-licensed authorized dealers, documented under a standard ISDA or bank master FX agreement; no CBS pre-approval is required for the WS_IC by virtue of the ICA exchange-control exemption.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and USD/WST) for term-matching of USD-denominated infrastructure costs against EUR/USD-denominated subscription receivables, documented under ISDA 2002 with CSA collateral arrangements and a board-approved non-speculative treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on WST via offshore bank desks for net WST exposure hedging only; permissible in principle under the IC exemption and subject to counterparty credit-line availability, given the thin onshore deliverable WST forward market.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form IC-AR) covering directors, members, registered office, registered agent and share capital particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days following each anniversary of incorporation; a 30-day extension may be granted by the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of USD 150 plus a monthly surcharge of 5% on the unpaid annual fee for each commenced month of default; continued failure for more than 12 months exposes the International Company to notice of administrative strike-off and eventual dissolution from the Samoa International Companies Register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Licence Fee Renewal on the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies / Samoa International Finance Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on each anniversary of incorporation; a grace period of 30 days applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic late fee of USD 100 if not paid by expiry of the grace period; monthly interest accrues at 1.5%; after six months of non-payment the registrar may initiate strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Agent and Registered Office Details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent for filing with the Registrar of International Companies, MCIL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrently with the Annual Return, within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unverified agent details render the company non-compliant under the International Companies Act; the Registrar may send a default notice and, after 60 days, appoint or require designation of a new registered agent at company expense

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit threshold applies to Samoa International Companies. A shareholder or group of shareholders holding at least 10% of voting rights may demand an independent audit; the Registrar may also order an audit in exceptional circumstances concerning public interest or suspected non-compliance.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or IFRS for Small and Medium-sized Entities, at the discretion of the directors; Samoa International Companies are not required to file audited financial statements with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Shareholdings are recorded in the Register of Members maintained at the registered office. Upon each transfer of shares, the registered agent must verify the board approval, update the Register of Members within 14 days, and amend the beneficial ownership information held by the licensed agent. At each annual renewal, the agent shall obtain a written confirmation of UBO status from each beneficial owner, and the agent is required to retain the confirmation for at least 5 years for AML/CFT inspection by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 – USD 1,200 per annum for a licensed Samoa registered agent and registered office service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 7,000 when an audit is voluntarily ordered or demanded by shareholders

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (Samoa International Company statutory exemption); general corporate rate is 27%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 100% exemption from income tax, capital gains tax and withholding tax on distributions under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); no payroll tax; no income tax on profit from international business operations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No income tax return is filed for exempt International Companies. Annual Government Fee remittance and 'Exempt Status Confirmation' filed through the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Online Companies Office portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before the anniversary of the date of incorporation; a grace period of 21 days is permitted in practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated annual renewal fee based on authorised share capital and company type
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs pay the same fee schedule and must provide registered agent confirmation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement confirming the registered office address in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be a physical address in Samoa; PO Box acceptable when combined with street address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of current directors and shareholders, including nominee if used
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No public beneficial ownership filing; register of directors maintained at registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the IC has not derived Samoan domestic sourced income, preserving tax-exempt status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be signed by the director or registered agent; false declaration attracts penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment of annual government fee incurs a penalty of WST 200 per month or part thereof; persistent non-payment may lead to strike-off and dissolution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for a tax-exempt International Company; general statutory rate is 15% for resident companies without exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Given the IC exemption, dividend withholding is not incurred and no DTA relief is generally needed. If the ordinary statutory rate were applicable, the taxpayer would submit the Corporate Income Tax Return with reduced WHT claim, attach the Samoa tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the Ministry of Revenue, and complete Form IR-100 (Treaty Relief Request) with the Samoan Revenue before distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates for non-residents: interest 10%, royalties 15%; for International Companies the IC Act exempts most payments to non-residents from withholding, allowing gross remittance of royalties and interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory TP documentation threshold applies to a tax-exempt IC. For taxable entities, the general transfer pricing documentation threshold is WST 20 million in annual turnover or related-party transactions exceeding WST 5 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's Economic Substance (International Companies) Regulations require tax-exempt ICs carrying on relevant activities (including software/SaaS operations potentially classified as intangible property or service centre activities) to demonstrate economic substance in Samoa or a qualifying jurisdiction, including board management, adequate staff, and expenditure. Compliance is evidenced through the annual IC registry return.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deriving income from Samoan domestic sources (e.g., providing payroll services to Samoan residents) while claiming international company tax exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disqualification of exempt status for the relevant year, assessment at the general 27% corporate rate, plus penalty tax of 20% and late payment interest at 1% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax if they knowingly enabled the misreport; civil restitution and personal liability orders apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a shell company with no employees, no office, and no genuine activity in Samoa or in a qualifying treaty partner jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Economic Substance Regulations, monetary penalty up to WST 500,000; possible compulsory strike-off; automatic exchange of information with partner tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally penalised for failing to appoint a qualified local director; travel bans and personal fines may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a registered agent or using the IC as a conduit for money laundering through payroll fund flows or to conceal beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-compliance with the International Companies Act leads to penalties of up to WST 100,000 and forfeiture of limited liability; criminal prosecution under the Financial Intelligence Unit Act carries imprisonment up to 14 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners involved in money laundering face asset confiscation, travel restrictions, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Adjusting prices with related parties without applying the arm's length standard (e.g., understating SaaS subscription revenue).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of additional tax at 27%, plus late-filing penalty of 20% of the adjusted profit; interest accrues at 1.5% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in the pricing decision may be jointly liable for the tax adjustment and separate criminal penalties for falsifying documents.
